newsitem.title: UK: IMF team advises Britain to raise taxes - newspaper.
newsitem.headline: IMF team advises Britain to raise taxes - newspaper.

text.p: Britain's ruling Labour Party will be advised by a team from the International Monetary Fund on Tuesday to raise taxes in order to cool the economy, said the Times newsaper.
The warning to British Chancellor of the Exchequer Gordon Brown includes urging him to consider extending value-added-tax to new areas, to dampen down consumer spending.
The IMF team also cast doubts over Labour's plan for a national minimum wage, saying that it would be a "blunt instrument," said the Times.

The team will also warn the government of looming imbalances in the economy, including surging domestic demand likely to be worsened by building society windfalls and the weakness of exports caused by the strength of sterling.

One of the central recommendations of the report will be that Brown adopt a more demanding target for public finances. The aim would be to produce more savings by the nation to release more resources for investment, said the paper.

However, the annual IMF inspection report will praise Brown's handling of the economy and conclude that his latest budget measures to combat demand were tougher than commentators appreciated and the sucession of interest rate rises was overdue.
The IMF team has spent the last 10 days talking to the Chancellor, Treasury, Bank of England officials and figures in London's financial district, said the newspaper.
